card.name: Passive verbs after a subject noun
card.fires_on: Forms of "to be" (is, are, was, be, been) and sometimes "benefits", placed right after a drug or thing name where a passive or adjective phrase follows, such as "is available" or "was authorized".

modes.label: Drug name then is/are
modes.description: The verb "is" or "are" right after a product name, often in capitals, in label text.

modes.label: Passive helper in general prose
modes.description: "was", "be" or "been" just before a past participle like authorized, used or conferred.
modes.example: The new law also required "that distinctive parcel post stamps must<< be>> used on all fourth-class matter beginning January

modes.label: Benefits conferred
modes.description: The word benefits (or BENEFITS) where "conferred" or "outweigh" comes next.

card.writes: It suppresses forms of "give", so the verb that follows is less likely to be give, gave or giving.
card.plain: It fires on "is", "was" or "been" after a subject, when the next word is likely a passive verb rather than "give".
